meanings.usage: 指任何能够伤害或杀死生物的物质
形容人的行为或想法缺乏逻辑性
指特别美味或珍贵的食物
描述让人觉得恶心或排斥的事物
一种海洋生物，常被当作食物
表达对某人或某事的强烈不喜欢或蔑视
形容特别珍贵或被珍视的东西，如prize plants获奖植物
指突然产生的强烈欲望或想法，如on impulse一时冲动
指因意外或失望而产生的震惊和沮丧感
指拥有或控制某物，take possession of表示接管、占领
指昂贵的享受或物品，a great luxury表示非常奢侈的享受
指把不同事物联系在一起，associate A with B把A和B联系起来
指从某处逃出来，或避免受到伤害
描述做某事时内心不愿意但又不得不做的状态

phrases.phrase: One man's meat is another man's poison
phrases.usage: 谚语，意思是甲之蜜糖，乙之砒霜。指不同的人对同一种事物有不同的喜好或评价

examples.en: One man's meat is another man's poison - some people love coffee but others find it terrible.
examples.zh: 萝卜青菜各有所爱——有人爱咖啡，有人却觉得它很糟糕。

phrases.usage: 坚持；坚守；维持原状。指坚持做某事或坚持某种习惯

examples.en: We stick to our original plan despite the difficulties.
examples.zh: 尽管有困难，我们仍然坚持原计划。

examples.en: Most people stick to the foods they grew up with.
examples.zh: 大多数人都坚持吃他们从小吃到大的食物。

phrases.usage: 吸引；使感兴趣。指某事物引起某人的兴趣或好感

examples.en: The idea never appealed to me very much.
examples.zh: 这个想法从来没有真正吸引过我。

examples.en: Does this job appeal to you?
examples.zh: 这份工作吸引你吗？

phrases.usage: 凭（一时）冲动。指突然产生的强烈欲望或想法驱使的行动

examples.en: Acting on a sudden impulse, I collected several dozen snails.
examples.zh: 一时冲动之下，我抓了几十只蜗牛。

examples.en: She bought the dress on impulse.
examples.zh: 她一时冲动买下了那条裙子。

phrases.usage: 拥有；接管；占领。指开始控制或占据某物

examples.en: The snails had taken complete possession of the hall!
examples.zh: 蜗牛已经完全占领了门厅！

examples.en: The company took possession of the new building last month.
examples.zh: 公司上个月接管了那栋新楼。

phrases.usage: 高兴做某事；对某事感到高兴。表达对某事的愉悦感受

examples.en: Robert was delighted to see me and equally pleased with my little gift.
examples.zh: 罗伯特见到我很高兴，对我的小礼物也很满意。

phrases.usage: 对...感到恶心/反胃。指对某种想法或气味感到厌恶

examples.en: Your stomach would turn at the idea of frying potatoes in animal fat.
examples.zh: 一想到用动物油炸土豆，你就会感到恶心。

phrases.usage: 抚养；培养；养大。指在成长过程中被照顾和教育

examples.en: Most of us have been brought up to eat certain foods.
examples.zh: 我们大多数人在成长过程中都被培养吃某些特定的食物。

phrases.usage: 一阵大雨；倾盆大雨。指短时间内的大降雨

examples.en: One day, after a heavy shower, I noticed a huge number of snails.
examples.zh: 有一天，一阵大雨过后，我注意到大量的蜗牛。

phrases.usage: 自从；从那以后一直。指从过去的某个时间点一直持续到现在

examples.en: There are countless people who, ever since their early years, have learned to associate snails with food.
examples.zh: 有无数人从童年时代起就学会把蜗牛和食物联系起来。

grammar.title: 过去进行时 (Past Continuous Tense)
grammar.definition: 过去进行时表示在过去某一时刻或某一段时间正在进行的动作。 用于描述在过去某个特定时刻正在发生的动作，或与另一个过去动作形成对比。本课中'I happened to be walking in my garden when I noticed...'描述了作者在大雨中正在花园里散步时看到了蜗牛。

examples.en: I happened to be walking in my garden when I noticed a huge number of snails.
examples.zh: 我碰巧在花园里散步时注意到大量的蜗牛。

examples.en: I was reading a book when he called.
examples.zh: 他打电话时我正在看书。

examples.en: She was cooking dinner at 7 o'clock yesterday evening.
examples.zh: 昨晚七点她正在做晚饭。

grammar.title: 间接宾语和直接宾语 (Indirect and Direct Objects)
grammar.structure: 主语 + 动词 + 间接宾语 + 直接宾语 或 主语 + 动词 + 直接宾语 + to/for + 间接宾语
grammar.definition: 某些动词可以带两个宾语：间接宾语（通常指人）和直接宾语（通常指物）。间接宾语通常位于直接宾语之前，但如果间接宾语放在后面，需要用介词to或for。 本课中'...I collected several dozen, put them in a paper bag, and took them to Robert.'展示了带两个宾语的用法。本课的被动语态结构也涉及宾语转换。

examples.en: I took them to Robert. (= I took Robert them.)
examples.zh: 我把它们带给了罗伯特。

examples.en: She bought me a gift. (= She bought a gift for me.)
examples.zh: 她给我买了一份礼物。

examples.en: Could you pass me the salt?
examples.zh: 你能把盐递给我吗？

grammar.title: 时间状语从句 (Adverbial Clause of Time)
grammar.definition: 时间状语从句用来说明动作发生的时间，由从属连词如when, while, after, before, as soon as等引导。 本课中多次使用时间状语从句，如'...when I noticed...', '...when Robert suddenly said...'等。when表示具体的时间点，while表示时间段。

examples.en: I was walking in my garden when I noticed a huge number of snails.
examples.zh: 我在花园里散步时，注意到大量的蜗牛。

examples.en: Robert and I went into the living room where we talked for a couple of hours.
examples.zh: 我和罗伯特走进客厅，在那里谈了两个小时。

examples.en: I had forgotten all about the snails when Robert suddenly said that I must stay to dinner.
examples.zh: 我已经完全忘了蜗牛这件事，这时罗伯特突然说我必须留下来吃晚饭。

patterns.pattern: No + 名词 + has received more...than...

original.en: No creature has received more praise and abuse than the common garden snail.
original.zh: 没有任何生物受到的赞扬和批评比得上普通的花园蜗牛。

imitations.en: No movie has received more praise and criticism than Titanic.
imitations.zh: 没有任何电影受到的赞扬和批评比得上《泰坦尼克号》。

imitations.en: No sport has received more attention than football in this country.
imitations.zh: 在这个国家，没有任何运动受到的关注比得上足球。

original.en: There are countless people who, ever since their early years, have learned to associate snails with food.
original.zh: 有无数人从童年时代起就学会把蜗牛和食物联系起来。

imitations.en: There are countless people who have learned to associate tea with relaxation.
imitations.zh: 有无数人学会把茶和放松联系起来。

imitations.en: There are countless people who, ever since their college days, have been working in this field.
imitations.zh: 有无数人从大学时代起就一直在这个领域工作。

patterns.pattern: 主语 + happened to be + doing + when...

original.en: I happened to be walking in my garden when I noticed a huge number of snails.
original.zh: 我碰巧在花园里散步时注意到大量的蜗牛。

imitations.en: She happened to be reading a book when the earthquake happened.
imitations.zh: 地震发生时她碰巧在看书。

imitations.en: I happened to be cooking dinner when the guests arrived.
imitations.zh: 客人到达时我碰巧在做晚饭。

patterns.pattern: 主语 + be delighted to + 动词原形

original.en: Robert was delighted to see me and equally pleased with my little gift.
original.zh: 罗伯特见到我很高兴，对我的小礼物也很满意。

imitations.en: My mother was delighted to hear the good news.
imitations.zh: 我妈妈听到这个好消息很高兴。

imitations.en: The children were delighted to receive the presents.
imitations.zh: 孩子们收到礼物很高兴。

text.title: One man's meat is another man's poison

lines.en: snails that made the writer collect them for his friend on that in particular?
lines.zh: 在决定什么能吃而什么不能吃的时候，人们往往变得不合情理。

lines.en: People become quite illogical when they try to decide what can be eaten and what cannot be eaten. If you lived in the Mediterranean , for instance, you would consider octopus a great delicacy .
lines.zh: 比如，如果你住在地中海地区，你会把章鱼视作是美味佳肴，同时不能理解为什么有人一见章鱼就恶心。

lines.en: You would not be able to understand why some people find it repulsive .
lines.zh: 另一方面，你一想到动物油炸土豆就会反胃，但这在北方许多国家却是一种普通的烹任方法。

lines.en: On the other hand, your stomach would turn at the idea of frying potatoes in animal fat -- the normally accepted practice in many northern countries.
lines.zh: 不无遗憾的是，我们中的大部分人，生来就只吃某几种食品，而且一辈子都这样。

lines.en: The sad truth is that most of us have been brought up to eat certain foods and we stick to them all our lives.
lines.zh: 没有一种生物所受到的赞美和厌恶会超过花园里常见的蜗牛了。

lines.en: No creature has received more praise and abuse than the common garden snail .
lines.zh: 蜗牛加酒烧煮后，便成了世界上许多地方的一道珍奇的名菜。

lines.en: Cooked in wine, snails are a great luxury in various parts of the world.
lines.zh: 有不计其数的人们从小就知道蜗牛可做菜。

lines.en: There are countless people who, ever since their early years, have learned to associate snails with food.
lines.zh: 但我的朋友罗伯特却住在一个厌恶蜗牛的国家中。

lines.en: My friend, Robert, lives in a country where snails are despised.
lines.zh: 他住在大城市里的一所公寓里，没有自己的花园。

lines.en: As his flat is in a large town, he has no garden of his own.
lines.zh: 多年来，他一直让我把我园子里的蜗牛收集起来给他捎去。

lines.en: For years he has been asking me to collect snails from my garden and take them to him.
lines.zh: 一开始，他的这一想法没有引起我多大兴趣。

lines.en: The idea never appealed to me very much, but one day, after heavy shower, I happened to be walking in my garden when I noticed a huge number of snails taking a stroll on some of my prize plants.
lines.zh: 后来有一天，一场大雨后，我在花园里漫无目的散步，突然注意到许许多多蜗牛在我的一些心爱的花木上慢悠悠的蠕动着。

lines.en: Acting on a sudden impulse, I collected several dozen, put them in a paper bag, and took them to Robert.
lines.zh: 我一时冲动，逮了几十只，装进一只纸袋里，带着去找罗伯特。

lines.en: Robert was delighted to see me and equally pleased with my little gift.
lines.zh: 罗伯特见到我很高兴，对我的薄礼也感到满意。

lines.en: I left the bag in the hall and Robert and I went into the living room where we talked for a couple of hours.
lines.zh: 我把纸袋放在门厅里，与罗伯特一起进了起居室，在那里聊了好几个钟头。

lines.en: I had forgotten all about the snails when Robert suddenly said that I must stay to dinner.
lines.zh: 我把蜗牛的事已忘得一干二净，罗伯特突然提出一定要我留下来吃晚饭，这才提醒了我。

lines.en: Snails would, of course, be the main dish.
lines.zh: 蜗牛当然是道主菜。

lines.en: I did not fancy the idea and I reluctantly followed Robert out of the room.
lines.zh: 我并不喜欢这个主意，所以我勉强跟着罗伯特走进了起居室。

lines.en: To our dismay, we saw that there were snails everywhere: they had escaped from the paper bag and had taken complete possession of the hall!
lines.zh: 使我们惊愕的是门厅里到处爬满了蜗牛：它们从纸袋里逃了出来，爬得满厅都是！

lines.en: I have never been able to look at a snail since then.
lines.zh: 从那以后，我再也不能看一眼蜗牛了。

questions.q: What was it about snails that made the writer collect them for his friend on that day in particular?
questions.zh: 究竟是什么原因，让作者在那一天特意为朋友收集了蜗牛？
questions.a: A heavy shower had just fallen, and while walking in his garden he noticed a huge number of snails taking a stroll on some of his prize plants. Acting on a sudden impulse, he collected several dozen and took them to Robert.
questions.aZh: 刚下过一场大雨，他在花园散步时发现许多蜗牛在他心爱的花木上爬动，一时冲动便逮了几十只送给罗伯特。
questions.hint: 答案出自 after heavy shower ... prize plants ... Acting on a sudden impulse 两句。

questions.q: What does the writer say people are like when they decide what can and cannot be eaten?
questions.zh: 作者说人们在决定什么能吃、什么不能吃时是什么样子？
questions.aZh: 人们往往变得不合情理。
questions.hint: 首句 People become quite illogical...

questions.q: How does the writer describe the common garden snail?
questions.zh: 作者如何描述常见的花园蜗牛？
questions.a: No creature has received more praise and abuse than the common garden snail.
questions.aZh: 没有一种生物受到的赞美和厌恶能超过花园里常见的蜗牛。
questions.hint: 见 No creature has received more praise and abuse than...

questions.q: Why did Robert ask the writer to bring him snails, and what happened to the snails in the hall?
questions.zh: 罗伯特为什么让作者给他带蜗牛？门厅里的蜗牛后来怎样了？
questions.a: Robert lives in a country where snails are despised, and as his flat is in a large town he has no garden of his own. When the two men came back, the snails had escaped from the paper bag and had taken complete possession of the hall.
questions.aZh: 罗伯特所住的国家厌恶蜗牛，他住在大城市的公寓里没有自己的花园。两人回来时，蜗牛已从纸袋逃出，爬满整个门厅。
questions.hint: 见 he has no garden of his own 与 took complete possession of the hall。

questions.q: Why could the writer never look at a snail again, and how does this fit the title?
questions.zh: 为什么作者此后再也不能看一眼蜗牛？这与标题有何呼应？
questions.a: The sight of the hall crawling with escaped snails was so disgusting that he was permanently put off them. This reflects the title: what Robert regards as a delicacy is poison to the writer.
questions.aZh: 满是逃窜蜗牛的门厅令他反胃，从此对蜗牛彻底失去胃口。这正呼应标题：罗伯特眼中的美味，在作者看来却如同毒药。
questions.hint: 结合末句 I have never been able to look at a snail since then 与谚语含义。

translation:
在决定什么能吃而什么不能吃的时候，人们往往变得不合情理。
比如，如果你住在地中海地区，你会把章鱼视作是美味佳肴，同时不能理解为什么有人一见章鱼就恶心。
另一方面，你一想到动物油炸土豆就会反胃，但这在北方许多国家却是一种普通的烹任方法。
不无遗憾的是，我们中的大部分人，生来就只吃某几种食品，而且一辈子都这样。
没有一种生物所受到的赞美和厌恶会超过花园里常见的蜗牛了。
蜗牛加酒烧煮后，便成了世界上许多地方的一道珍奇的名菜。
有不计其数的人们从小就知道蜗牛可做菜。
但我的朋友罗伯特却住在一个厌恶蜗牛的国家中。
他住在大城市里的一所公寓里，没有自己的花园。
多年来，他一直让我把我园子里的蜗牛收集起来给他捎去。
一开始，他的这一想法没有引起我多大兴趣。
后来有一天，一场大雨后，我在花园里漫无目的散步，突然注意到许许多多蜗牛在我的一些心爱的花木上慢悠悠的蠕动着。
我一时冲动，逮了几十只，装进一只纸袋里，带着去找罗伯特。
罗伯特见到我很高兴，对我的薄礼也感到满意。
我把纸袋放在门厅里，与罗伯特一起进了起居室，在那里聊了好几个钟头。
我把蜗牛的事已忘得一干二净，罗伯特突然提出一定要我留下来吃晚饭，这才提醒了我。
蜗牛当然是道主菜。
我并不喜欢这个主意，所以我勉强跟着罗伯特走进了起居室。
使我们惊愕的是门厅里到处爬满了蜗牛：它们从纸袋里逃了出来，爬得满厅都是！
从那以后，我再也不能看一眼蜗牛了。
title: One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison
subtitle: 各有所爱

lead.question: 作者一向对收集蜗牛送朋友不感兴趣，为何偏在那天动了手？结果如何？
lead.warmup: 课文从一句英语谚语谈起：对一方有利的未必对另一方也有利，即“各有所爱”。人在决定什么能吃、什么不能吃时往往很不合情理：地中海人视章鱼为美味，北方人却爱用动物油煎土豆。接着他讲了蜗牛的故事——住在大城市公寓里的朋友罗伯特偏偏视蜗牛为珍馐，请他收集蜗牛捎来，结果一袋蜗牛在门厅里闹出大笑话。
goals: 理解谚语 One man's meat is another man's poison 的含义与用法。
掌握 delicacy、repulsion/repulsive、appeal to、stick to 等词的搭配。
学习过去分词作状语（Cooked in wine…）与虚拟条件句（If you lived…）。
能用英语复述作者为罗伯特收集蜗牛、蜗牛逃满门厅的故事。
lead.summary: 本文是一篇围绕“各有所爱”的幽默小品。作者先指出人在饮食上极不合逻辑：甲之美味可能正是乙之毒药。接着聚焦蜗牛——它在许多地方是酒烹名菜，在罗伯特的国家却遭人厌恶。罗伯特住公寓没有花园，多年托作者收集蜗牛。一个雨后，作者一时冲动逮了几十只送去，谁知蜗牛从纸袋逃出爬满门厅，成了主菜前的“惊喜”。
lead.tips: Cooked in wine 是过去分词短语作状语，表示条件，相当于 If they are cooked in wine，不要误当成谓语；另注意 repulse 是动词、repulsive 是形容词，find it repulsive 中须用形容词。

exercises.q: 汉译英：对一方有利的未必对另一方也有利。（用本课谚语）
exercises.a: One man's meat is another man's poison.

exercises.q: 汉译英：你会把章鱼视作一道美味佳肴。
exercises.a: You would consider octopus a great delicacy.
exercises.note: consider sth a delicacy 结构

exercises.q: 改错：People become quite illogic when they try to decide what can be eaten.
exercises.a: People become quite illogical when they try to decide what can be eaten.

exercises.q: 句型转换：用 appeal 改写 The idea never interested me very much.
exercises.a: The idea never appealed to me very much.
exercises.note: appeal to sb 意为吸引

exercises.q: 填空：You would not be able to understand why some people find it ______ (repulse).
填空：The sad truth is that most of us ______ (bring up) to eat certain foods and we ______ (stick) to them all our lives.
exercises.note: 现在完成时 + stick to 坚持

exercises.q: 句型转换：用 although 合并——Snails are a great luxury in many parts of the world. In Robert's country they are despised.
exercises.a: Although snails are a great luxury in many parts of the world, they are despised in Robert's country.
exercises.note: although 引导让步状语从句

quiz.q: 在决定什么能吃、什么不能吃时，人们往往变得怎样？
quiz.note: 首句 illogical 点明主题

quiz.q: 在地中海地区，人们如何看待章鱼？
作者说我们中大部分人一辈子都怎样看待某些食物？
在罗伯特所住的国家，蜗牛受到怎样的对待？
options: They are cherished as a luxury.
They are fried in animal fat.

quiz.q: 作者为什么在那天特意收集蜗牛送给罗伯特？
options: The idea had always appealed to him.
Robert had written to ask for them.
He wanted to sell them at the market.
He acted on a sudden impulse after seeing them on his prize plants.

quiz.q: 两人回到门厅时看到了什么？
options: The snails had escaped and taken complete possession of the hall.
Robert had already cooked the snails in wine.
The paper bag was still neatly closed.
A neighbour had taken the snails away.
quiz.note: take possession of 意为占据
